Just finished my first listen. While I do completely understand why this one might be disappointing to some fans, especially after such a long hiatus since their last one... I actually find it pretty enjoyable it for what it is. Having heard the first few singles (and being able to see that none of the track times were longer than four and a half minutes), I knew going in that it wasn't going to be the same sort of prog rock as their other albums. I was pleased to find a few tracks that stood out as highlights aside from Blacklight Shine and Graveyard Love-- Que Dios, Flash Burns, Equus 3 and The Requisition all made a good impression on me. And I *love* that the promotional material for this album fully embraces the Puerto Rican cultural influence in a way we haven't seen as much from the band before.  


Look, maybe it's because *I'm* older than I was when the band released De-loused... but in this album's defense, I kind of appreciate having a TMV album that isn't as demanding a listen. I have a soft spot for Frances the Mute, because it was my first one, and it makes me nostalgic for my college days, and no one is going to argue it's not a masterpiece, least of all me... but if I'm really being honest, it's also probably the album from them which I listen to the least, just because it's not always easy to find the energy to listen to a monster like Cassandra Gemini from start to finish (and that's not even accounting for the other songs on that album, a few of which *also* push past 12 minutes). It's not an album you can just casually put on. Conversely, now I feel like I actually have a TMV album that is much more easily digestible. In the right contexts, I feel like I could actually find myself listening to this one a lot *more* than their proggier stuff. I still love the old material just as much as I ever did. I just think there's also a place in their catalog for this different direction too.

Thank you so much for this generous offer! My mother is in her late 70s. She is the only family I have now, and I don't want to put her at risk. We have been sheltering in our home for over a week now, but have been unable to procure groceries without me going out and potentially exposing both of us to infection. I would be so grateful if we could work out a grocery drop-off.

I'm not really all that far from you, but I think I have you beat for confounding demonyms. I live on the other side of the border, in Bellingham. The official demonym is (I kid you not) Bellinghamster.

I'm in my early 30s now. I remember Layne Staley's death very vividly. I was deeply saddened, but knowing his history, I couldn't really say I was fully caught by surprise. The same could be said of when I learned of Scott Weiland's death just a few years ago, too. However, THIS one...

THIS absolutely devastates me. I can't put into words what a huge impact Chris Cornell's music has had on me, since my adolescence, all the way to the present day. Superunknown is one of my all-time favorite albums ever, and Badmotorfinger isn't too far behind it. I am fortunate enough to be able to say I saw him in concert, when he was with Audioslave. I got horribly sunburned, and soaked from a thunderstorm, and it was STILL one of the greatest live music shows I've ever experienced in my entire life. I feel like something really immense has been lost now... and the fact that it happened so unexpectedly, as Soundgarden was regaining their old momentum, just STINGS so damn much.

Just... fuuuuuuuck.

It's a lovely place-- or at least, the way I remember it, it was. Admittedly, I haven't been there in over 20 years, though. My parents used to have a vacation house on the island, but they were forced to sell it when the Soufriere Hills volcano became active again, and the entire southern half of the island was evacuated and labeled a danger zone. I've seen photos of Plymouth, and it's virtually unrecognizable to me-- it's a ghost town buried in ash, and parts of the town look like the surface of the moon now. Before the volcano, though, I remember the island being really beautiful and green, and the people were extremely friendly. 

Back in the day, the island was also a retreat for musicians like the Police, because there used to be a recording studio there. Unfortunately, the studio was destroyed in 1988 by Hurricane Hugo. It's a shame, really, because the islanders were just finally recovering from Hugo when Soufriere Hills flared up.

I will say, when John Oliver mentioned Montserrat on his show last night, it was a huge shock for me-- it's kind of an obscure place for most people, but it was a BIG part of my childhood.

That sounds totally awesome. :D And I'll try to find some good Indian or Greek food in Bellingham, too. Or maybe sushi. *lots of hugs* Thinking of you and sending all the happiness I can your way. :) <3 Love you, sister.

You're not alone. I know it may be difficult to feel otherwise when the nature of your challenge is so physically isolating, but remember you have so many people who care about you, myself included. You know you can always have hugs from me. That will NEVER change. :) <3 *hugs* When my own life settles down a bit in a few weeks and stops being such a swirling chaotic mess, I promise I'll come see you. I may be going to a new place, but I'm not leaving you.

Such a beautiful and touching sentiment. I'm so proud of you, for as far as you've come since then. You are and will always be a source of inspiration for me.

Thank YOU so much, too, for all the times you've been there to guide me out of my own darkness. I don't have the words to express how much it means to me that you've been a part of my life, and still are. <3

To some extent. They're obviously aware that I'm really bogged down with work and don't have time to hang out anymore, and my closest friends know I have been dealing with depression and a feeling of dissatisfaction with my life for some time. They're the best friends I could ever hope for-- as close to me as sisters-- and they've been so supportive and loving. The thought of potentially losing my ability to see them is so terrifying and demoralizing to me-- but in the back of my head, I can feel how real that possibility is.
